title: Per-key & per-route debug UX notes and mock flows (SLO-aware quotas)
body:
Purpose
This note collects sketches, edge cases, and prioritized backlog items for a debugging-first UX for per-key and per-route usage pages. Goal: make it fast for SREs, platform engineers, and paying product teams to answer the three questions they actually care about when a quota or rate-limit alert fires: (1) who/what is being throttled, (2) why (pattern + rule), and (3) how to mitigate quickly.

Context and constraints
- Existing console shows aggregate quota charts and an exportable CSV. Users have asked for faster drilldowns and for actionable mitigations (e.g., temporary overrides, canary reroute).
- Data model: events stream with credential id, route id, tokens consumed, response latency, outcome (200/4xx/5xx/429), model variant, region, timestamp. Not all fields are guaranteed for older logs.
- Performance: detail panels must load in <2s for 30 days window; heavy queries should sample or use precomputed rollups.
- Security: per-key details are only visible to owners/org admins; masking for cross-team views.

Primary audiences
- Platform engineers: need to triage capacity hotspots and see per-route cost delta when switching quantization/batching suggestions.
- Product/engineers owning features: need to map keys to product features and see UX impact (user-visible errors).
- SRE/Support: need to produce incident timeline and suggested mitigations to return to service level.

Design principles
- Debugging-first: show failure and throttle signals before overall totals.
- Actionability: expose quick mitigation buttons (increase quota, create fallback route, apply short-term exemption) guarded by RBAC.
- Progressive disclosure: summary row -> time-series -> sample requests -> raw event viewer.
- Explainability: surface which quota/rate-rule triggered and why (e.g., token burst > 10k in 1m).

Screens and interactions (wireframe writeups)
1) Top-level Key Overview (list/grid)
- Columns: credential id (masked), owner, plan tier, current quota window usage %, active rate-limit status (ok/warning/throttled), SLO risk indicator (green/amber/red).
- Quick actions on row hover: Open Key Detail, Open Incident Draft, Create Temporary Override (modal), Add to Watchlist.
- Mini inline sparkline for last 24h QPS and a tiny stacked bar showing error composition (200/4xx/5xx/429).
- Sorting defaults: throttled first, then SLO risk.

2) Key Detail panel (left split) -> Route Breakdown (right split)
- Left: header with key metadata (plan, created, linked repos, owner contact). One-line computed summary: "3 routes contribute 78% of tokens; 2 routes produce 90% of 429s".
- Right: list of top routes for this key with columns: route path, tokens, avg latency, 429 rate, 5xx rate, predominant model variant. Each route row is clickable to expand route timeline inline.
- Inline expansion shows 1h heatmap + 5 sampled example requests (request headers masked per policy) with token counts and response body excerpt. Sample selection strategy: latest failed, highest tokens, random sample.

3) Route Timeline and Failure Decomposition
- Top: time series with stacked areas: tokens, successful requests, 429s, 5xxs (normalized). Overlay quota threshold lines and SLO band (target/alert). Hover shows queryable buckets (1m, 5m, 1h).
- Middle: event waterfall for the selected window showing burst patterns and correlated latency spikes.
- Bottom: root-cause hints (generated heuristics): "bursty retries from IP X: showing 2.3k calls in 10m; likely SDK misconfiguration" or "sustained token consumption increase after deploy: commit abc123" (link to GitHub if available).

4) Quota & Rate Rule Explanation panel (drawer)
- When a throttle is detected, show the exact rule: window, burst allowance, token weighting, route-level exceptions. If multiple rules interact, show precedence. Provide a tiny decision graph (text lines) explaining which rule matched the sample event.
- Suggest mitigations ranked by expected impact & risk: small-handed quick fixes (reduce client QPS, short override), medium (apply route whitelist for internal traffic), larger (request plan bump). Each suggestion has an estimated token/cost delta and time-to-effect.

5) Mitigation Controls (RBAC guarded)
- Temporary override modal: duration (15m, 1h, 6h), scope (key, route, region), reason (free text), estimated cost impact preview. Record as an audit event.
- Canary reroute composer: pick fallback model/region and set percentage of traffic for N minutes. Preview expected per-token latency and cost.

6) Raw Request Drill and Reproduction Playbook
- "Reproduce this sample" button that builds a cURL/snippet (masked secrets) and a small checklist: reproduce -> confirm -> mitigation. Include a copyable block for SRE runbook.
- Export button: download sample set (csv/json) with redaction applied.

Data and UX tradeoffs noted
- Full fidelity vs speed: for 90-day queries we show rollups and sample-based request lists; for 7-day windows provide near-complete raw events.
- Cost signal compute: token accounting is heavier than raw count; precompute rolling windows nightly and provide last-5m near-real-time delta using streaming aggregator.
- Sampling bias: surface sampling strategy prominently and allow toggle to "prefer high-token samples" vs "prefer errors".

Backlog (prioritized)
- P0: Key Overview + Key Detail + quick actions (override, watchlist) – proof-of-concept with mocked sampling API.
- P1: Route Inline Expansion + 5-sample viewer + time-series overlays + quota rule explanation drawer.
- P2: Mitigation controls wired to backend + audit logs + RBAC + cost preview API.
- P3: Canary reroute composer and impact simulator + integration to releases metadata (link commits to user-visible spikes).
- P4: Automatic RCA hints using correlation heuristics + Slack incident draft automation.

Acceptance criteria (for P0 -> P1)
- Key Overview lists keys and shows usage % and active throttle state; load time < 1.8s for orgs with <=5k keys.
- Clicking Open Key Detail shows top 10 routes and an inline expansion sample; expansion loads in <1s using sampling endpoint.
- Override flow opens modal and performs a dry-run showing cost impact without committing when user selects "preview".

Open questions / design risks
- Privacy: what fields must be redacted from request samples by default? (user ids, email, PII). Decision affects usefulness of sample snippets.
- RBAC: should support delegated support engineers who can create temporary overrides but not permanent plan changes? Implementation complexity around audit trails.
- Interaction with Dedicated/Private deployments: telemetry availability differs; need graceful fallback text when no raw events are accessible.

Next steps and owners
- Asha: prototype Top-level Key Overview HTML table with mock data (2 weeks).
- Diego: backend sampling API contract: /keys/:id/samples?window=&strategy= (1 week).
- Priya: design microcopy for quota explanation drawer and override modal (3 days).
- Evan: perf constraints and precompute plan for token windows (sync with infra) (1 week).

Notes to reviewer
- This is deliberately pragmatic: early build focuses on surfacing why the throttle happened, not perfect visual polish.
- Please flag any missing RBAC states we should model and any privacy guardrails.

Appendix: quick ASCII wireframe for Key Detail (very rough)
[Key header] | [Top routes table (rows)]
---------------------------------------------
| key: rwd-•••• | route1  | tokens | 429% | expand >
| owner: acme   | route2  | tokens | 429% | expand >
| plan: growth  | route3  | tokens | 429% | expand >
---------------------------------------------
Expanded row -> inline timeline (small chart) + sample list (timestamp, token_count, status)

End of doc.
